device.model: RP2DAQ board on Raspberry Pi Pico
device.name: RP2DAQ board (rp2daq.Rp2daq)

facts.text: Rp2daq is the user-facing object that owns the board connection and delegates the protocol to Rp2daq_internals
The command methods are generated from the C firmware at construction and attached to the Rp2daq object with setattr; the Python class itself defines only quit
quit stops the report threads and asks the backend process to release the serial port
gpio_out connects the selected pin directly to 0 V or 3.3 V and overrides a previous high-Z or pull state
gpio_in returns the digital state of a pin; the maximum allowed voltage at any pin is 3.3 V
adc samples the built-in 12-bit ADC and returns a report whose data field is the sample array
pwm_configure_pair sets the wrap value and clock divider of a PWM slice; pwm_set_value sets the duty value of one GPIO
stepper_init configures an A4988-compatible stepper; the endswitch input is documented as a safety and convenience measure
stepper_move moves a stepper to a target in nanosteps (1/256 microstep); speed is in nanosteps per 100 microseconds and its accepted range is 1 to 10000
stepper_status returns the position, the endswitch state and three 16-bit bitmasks for all 16 steppers
The 12-bit ADC range is about 0 V at count 0 and about 3.2 V at count 4095
The firmware identifies its USB serial port by VID:PID 2E8A:000A on RP2040 or 2E8A:0009 on RP2350
The upstream README drives GPIO 25, the green onboard LED, with gpio_out
The adc defaults are channel_mask=1, blocksize=1000, clkdiv=95 and trigger_gpio=-1
Issuing stepper_move to an already moving stepper stops it immediately
With relative set to 1 the move is relative to the position of the motor when the command is issued

measures.description: Mean raw count of one 12-bit ADC block on channel 0 (0 to 4095; README.md:100 relates it approximately to volts)
measures.name: adc_mean

measures.description: Position of stepper 0 in nanosteps (1/256 microstep)
measures.name: stepper_position

measures.description: True while stepper 0 has a target different from its current position
measures.name: stepper_moving

operator_required.name: stepper_move
operator_required.reason: the firmware bounds the position only against a 32-bit overflow (about -2_147_000_000 to 2_147_000_000 nanosteps, include/stepper.c:245); the travel of the mechanism a stepper drives is the site's, so the site supplies the range

safe_state.description: every initialized stepper is held at its current position, PWM outputs are zero and configured GPIO outputs are low
